examples.en: This towel is for guests, so please don't use it.
The guest slippers are next to the entrance.
There isn't a single guest blanket at home.

examples.ko: 이 방은 평소에는 비어 있고 손님용으로만 써요.
examples.en: This room is usually empty and only used for guests.

examples.ko: 화장실에 손님용 칫솔이 새것으로 준비돼 있어요.
examples.en: A new toothbrush for guests is ready in the bathroom.

examples.ko: 이건 우리가 먹는 거예요? 아니면 손님용이에요?
examples.en: Is this for us to eat? Or is it for guests?

explain: '-용'은 '어린이용', '여성용'처럼 누가 쓰는지 알려 주는 말이에요. '손님용'은 한 단어라서 붙여 써요. 반대로 우리 식구가 쓰는 것은 '가족용'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '-용' tells who something is meant for, as in '어린이용' and '여성용'. '손님용' is one word, so write it without a space. Things for your own household can be called '가족용'.

examples.ko: 이 찻잔은 접대용이라서 평소에는 안 써요.
examples.en: This teacup is for entertaining guests, so I don't use it usually.

examples.ko: 접대용 선물은 너무 비싸지 않은 게 좋아요.
examples.en: A gift for entertaining guests shouldn't be too expensive.
I put a new sofa for receiving guests in the living room.

examples.ko: 회사 손님이 오면 접대용 과자를 내요.
examples.en: When company guests come, we serve snacks meant for them.
I bought this set of dishes for entertaining guests.
The office keeps separate coffee for entertaining guests.

explain: '손님용'은 손님이 쓰는 물건이고, '접대용'은 손님을 대접하려고 준비한 것이에요. 회사 손님을 맞을 때도 써요. '접대용 멘트'처럼 겉으로만 예의를 차리는 말을 가리키기도 해요.
explain_en: '손님용' is for things guests use, while '접대용' is for things prepared to treat guests. It is also used when receiving business guests. In '접대용 멘트', it refers to words said only for show.

examples.ko: 호텔 방을 예약했는데요. 몇 시부터 체크인할 수 있어요?
examples.en: I booked a hotel room. From what time can I check in?

examples.ko: 체크인하실 때 예약 확인서를 보여 주세요.
examples.en: Please show your booking confirmation when you check in.

examples.ko: 비행기가 늦어서 밤 열두 시에야 체크인했어요.
examples.en: My flight was late, so I only checked in at midnight.

examples.ko: 먼저 체크인하고 짐을 방에 둔 다음에 구경해요.
examples.en: Let's check in first, leave our bags in the room, and then look around.

examples.ko: 온라인으로 미리 체크인하면 줄을 안 서도 돼요.
examples.en: If you check in online beforehand, you don't have to wait in line.

examples.ko: 일행이 아직 안 와서 제가 대신 체크인해도 될까요?
examples.en: My group hasn't arrived yet, so may I check in for them?

explain: 반대말은 '체크아웃하다'예요. 호텔뿐 아니라 공항에서도 쓰고, '체크인 시간이 몇 시예요?'처럼 '체크인'만 명사로도 말해요. 호텔 직원은 손님에게 '체크인하실 때'처럼 높여서 말해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '체크아웃하다'. It is used at airports as well as hotels, and '체크인' alone works as a noun, as in '체크인 시간이 몇 시예요?'. Hotel staff speak politely to guests, as in '체크인하실 때'.

examples.en: I like sake.

examples.ko: 일식집에서 따뜻한 사케를 한 병 시켰어요.
examples.en: At the Japanese restaurant I ordered a bottle of warm sake.

examples.ko: 여행 가서 기념품으로 사케를 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I went on a trip and bought sake as a souvenir.
This sake tastes best when it is served cold.

examples.ko: 사케 한 잔에 초밥을 같이 먹었어요.
examples.en: I had sushi along with a glass of sake.

examples.ko: 사케 종류가 많아서 뭘 고를지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: There are many kinds of sake, so I don't know which to pick.

explain: 일본어에서 온 말이고, 한국에서는 일본식 청주를 가리킬 때 많이 써요. 예전에는 '정종'이라고도 불렀어요. 주로 일식집이나 일본 여행 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: It comes from Japanese, and in Korea it mostly refers to Japanese-style refined rice wine. It used to be called '정종' as well. It mainly comes up at Japanese restaurants or when talking about trips to Japan.

examples.ko: 주말에 친구랑 하이볼을 한 잔 마셔요.
examples.en: On the weekend I have a highball with a friend.
The lemon highball is popular at this shop.
Please put a lot of ice in the highball.
A highball has soda in it, so it's very refreshing.
I like juice more than a highball.

examples.ko: 새로 나온 메뉴판에 하이볼 종류가 많아요.
examples.en: The new menu has many kinds of highballs.

explain: 위스키 같은 술에 탄산수를 섞은 음료예요. '레몬 하이볼', '진저 하이볼'처럼 앞에 맛이나 재료를 붙여 말해요. 주문할 때는 '하이볼 한 잔 주세요'처럼 '잔'으로 세요.
explain_en: It is a drink made by mixing spirits such as whisky with soda water. You put the flavor or ingredient in front, as in '레몬 하이볼' and '진저 하이볼'. When ordering, count it by '잔', as in '하이볼 한 잔 주세요'.

examples.en: I go to a pub with my friends on Friday evening.

examples.ko: 이 펍은 분위기가 좋고 음악이 좋아요.
examples.en: This pub has a nice atmosphere and good music.
We watched the soccer game together at a pub.
A new pub opened near my office.
This pub's menu also has French fries.

examples.ko: 저는 펍보다 조용한 카페가 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like a quiet cafe more than a pub.

explain: '펍'은 영어 pub에서 온 말로 서양식 분위기의 술집을 말해요. 일반적인 술집은 '술집'이라고 하고, 한국식 맥줏집은 '호프'라고도 불러요. 보통 '펍에 가다', '펍에서 만나다'처럼 장소로 써요.
explain_en: '펍' comes from the English word pub and means a bar with a Western-style atmosphere. A general drinking place is a '술집', and a Korean-style beer place is also called a '호프'. It is usually used as a place, as in '펍에 가다' and '펍에서 만나다'.

examples.en: I have preview homework for tomorrow's class.
Preview time is usually thirty minutes.
I do the preparation before class.
I prepare the words on the subway.
The students prepare and then come to class.

explain: 예습은 수업 전에 미리 보는 거예요. 예습, 예약, 예매의 ‘예’는 모두 ‘미리’라는 뜻이에요.

dict_examples.en: Do your preview and review thoroughly.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The teacher emphasized the importance of preparing for lessons.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 예습 means looking at the lesson ahead of time. The 예 in 예습, 예약 (reservation) and 예매 (advance ticket) all carries the idea of “beforehand”.

examples.en: I was busy all day entertaining guests.

examples.ko: 거래처 사람들을 접대해야 해서 오늘 저녁에 약속이 있어요.
examples.en: I have to entertain clients, so I have plans this evening.

examples.ko: 부장님이 손님을 접대하는 자리에 저도 갔어요.
examples.en: I also went to the dinner where our department head was hosting a guest.
We hosted the relatives who came to our house with great care.
I started preparing the food to serve the guests in the morning.
We keep the costs of entertaining at the company in a separate record.

explain: '대접하다'는 가족이나 친구에게도 쓰지만, '접대하다'는 일 때문에 만난 손님이나 거래처를 모실 때 자주 써요. 그래서 회사 이야기에 많이 나와요. '접대비', '접대 자리'처럼 단어를 붙여서도 써요.
explain_en: '대접하다' can be used for family and friends too, but '접대하다' is often used for guests or business partners you meet for work, so it appears a lot in office talk. It also forms words such as '접대비' (entertainment expenses) and '접대 자리' (an entertaining occasion).

examples.en: That dog died last winter.

examples.ko: 물을 안 줘서 화분의 꽃이 죽었어요.
examples.en: I didn't water it, so the flower in the pot died.

examples.ko: 겨울에 너무 추워서 정원의 나무가 죽었어요.
examples.en: It was so cold in winter that the tree in the garden died.
The fish died, and the child cried a lot.
A dead tree has no leaves.

explain: 사람이 세상을 떠났을 때는 보통 ‘돌아가셨어요’라고 말해요. ‘죽었어요’는 동물이나 식물에 많이 써요.

phrases.en: to be dying of ~, so ~ (strong exaggeration)
phrases.nuance_en: a strong exaggeration meaning something is extremely intense, as in 더워 죽겠다
phrases.en_equiv: to be dying of ~, so ~ (strong exaggeration)

phrases.nuance_en: used when you do something with all your strength, as if your life depended on it

explain_en: When a person has passed away, people usually say 돌아가셨어요. 죽었어요 is more common for animals and plants.

p.n: 숨지다 sounds like a news report; 죽다 is plain and direct.

examples.en: During rush hour the subway is packed.
My commute takes two hours a day.
I read a book on the bus when I commute.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 회사에서 가까워서 출퇴근이 편해요.
examples.en: My house is close to the office, so commuting is easy.
How do you commute? — I walk.

explain: ‘출근’은 일하러 가는 것, ‘퇴근’은 일이 끝나고 돌아가는 것이에요. ‘출퇴근’은 이 두 가지를 합친 말이에요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 출근 is going to work and 퇴근 is leaving work to go home. 출퇴근 puts the two together.

examples.en: Shall we study together? — Sure.

examples.ko: 내일 점심 같이 먹을까요? — 네, 그래요.
examples.en: Shall we have lunch together tomorrow? — Sure, sounds good.
Tomorrow is my birthday. — Really? Happy birthday!

examples.ko: 오늘 정말 추워요. — 네, 그래요. 커피 마실까요?
examples.en: It's really cold today. — Yes, it is. Shall we have some coffee?

examples.ko: 토요일 저녁에 만날까요? — 그래요. 일곱 시 어때요?
examples.en: Shall we meet on Saturday evening? — Okay. How about seven?

explain: 끝을 올려서 “그래요?” 하면 ‘정말요?’라는 뜻이에요. 끝을 내려서 “그래요.” 하면 ‘좋아요’나 ‘맞아요’라는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: With rising intonation, “그래요?” means “Really?”. With falling intonation, “그래요.” means “Okay” or “That's right”.

examples.en: My dream is to be a businessperson.
My uncle is a businessman who runs a small company.

examples.ko: 그 사업가는 작은 가게에서 시작해서 큰 회사를 만들었어요.
examples.en: That businessman started in a small shop and built a big company.
My friend is famous as a young entrepreneur.
You need courage to become a businessperson.

explain: ‘사장’은 회사에서 가장 높은 자리고, ‘사업가’는 사업을 하는 사람이에요. 작은 가게 주인을 ‘사장님’이라고 부르지만, 보통 ‘사업가’라고 하지는 않아요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 아버지는 망해 가는 기업을 인수해서 다시 일으킨, 유능한 사업가이시다.
dict_examples.en: My father is a capable businessman who took over a failing company and revived it.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 사장 is the top position in a company; 사업가 is a person who does business. A small shop owner is called 사장님, but usually not 사업가.

examples.en: It's Spanish.
Spanish class is on Monday.
My younger sibling is learning Spanish.
In Mexico they use Spanish.
Do you speak Spanish well?

explain: 스페인 + 어 = 스페인어. 멕시코나 아르헨티나 사람도 스페인어를 쓰지만 '멕시코어'라고 하지 않아요.
explain_en: 스페인 + 어 = Spanish. People in Mexico or Argentina speak Spanish too, but nobody says '멕시코어'.
